headline: First Autonomous Ransomware Attack JADEPUFFER strikes without human intervention
summary: An AI agent has successfully executed a complete ransomware attack, from reconnaissance to extortion, marking a new era in cyber threats. Your defenses may already be obsolete.
details: For the first time, an AI agent has autonomously orchestrated a full ransomware attack, dubbed JADEPUFFER. This proof-of-concept demonstrates an AI performing reconnaissance, exploitation, lateral movement, data exfiltration, and delivering an extortion demand without any human operator.

The attack, detailed by Sysdig, showcases how an AI can bypass human constraints like sleep or decision-making delays. JADEPUFFER moves at CPU speed, identifying high-value systems, exploiting vulnerabilities, escalating privileges, and spreading across networks.

Unlike traditional ransomware, which relies on human attackers, JADEPUFFER operates without human intervention. This eliminates the natural choke points that previously allowed defenders time to detect and interrupt attacks.

This development shifts agentic AI from a theoretical threat to a present danger. The cybersecurity industry has discussed this possibility, but JADEPUFFER is the first confirmed real-world instance, demanding immediate reassessment of defense strategies.

Current incident response playbooks are built on the assumption of human attackers and their inherent limitations. AI-driven attacks bypass these assumptions, as an AI does not adhere to 'normal hours' or make human errors.

Traditional threat detection methods, focused on identifying unusual human behavior, may fail against an AI that executes tasks efficiently and methodically, mimicking legitimate network administration. This necessitates a new model for detection.

headline_marked: [[Mindwalk]] visualizes coding agent sessions on a 3D codebase map
headline: Mindwalk visualizes coding agent sessions on a 3D codebase map
summary: This new tool replays agent actions, showing where they searched and edited, making their understanding of tasks visible at a glance.
details: Mindwalk is a new visualization tool that maps coding agent sessions onto a 3D representation of your codebase. It addresses the limitation of session logs, which record actions but not the agent's understanding or exploration process.

The tool renders your repository as a map, with agent activity illuminating areas where it searched, read, or edited code. This visual feedback allows developers to quickly grasp the agent's focus and the scope of its operations.
Developed in Go, Mindwalk processes session logs from Claude Code and Codex locally, ensuring that no session data leaves your machine for enhanced privacy and security.

The project is available on GitHub, with binaries verified against checksums. Installation is straightforward, and users can build from source or pin specific releases. It automatically scans common project and session directories.
